body.Project Name: Sterling EDI to SAP Integration Suite
body.Report Name: 03.25.2026 Sterling EDI to SAP Integration Suite
body.Accomplished Activities:
The EDI Migration initiative has progressed significantly on the decision and planning front, with clarity now established on the available forward paths, their financial impact, and associated risks.

Scenario analysis completed and socialized: A comprehensive impact assessment was completed outlining three viable paths forward—IT Resonance–led, internal‑only with commercial tenant, and internal‑only NS2‑only—clearly articulating timeline risk, resource burden, audit exposure, and financial consequences under each option.
End‑of‑year constraint clearly defined: The December 31, 2026 SAP Integration Suite free‑license deadline has been validated as a hard constraint and documented as the primary forcing function for the project.
Financial exposure quantified and escalated:

A clear cost comparison has been documented: ~$30K to fund the IT Resonance SOW now versus $150K in unplanned SAP licensing costs if the migration does not complete by year‑end.
The funding gap resulting from the 2025 cost‑center budget not carrying forward into 2026 has been reviewed with Brian and Greg and formally escalated.


Dependencies and decision owners identified:

Legal approval for use of the SAP commercial tenant (Mike Bokermann) has been confirmed as a critical path item across all scenarios.
IT Resonance funding (Dennis / Finance) has been isolated as the primary determinant between low‑risk and high‑risk execution paths.


Recommended path clearly articulated: Scenario 1 (fund IT Resonance, use commercial tenant now, transition to NS2 in Q3) has been formally recommended based on:

Ability to meet the year‑end deadline
Lowest overall delivery and audit risk
Preservation of internal team capacity


Risks documented with no ambiguity: Single‑point‑of‑failure risks on Johnny, SOX and KPMG audit obligations, TPM delays, and partner revenue exposure (Walmart, Academy) have been explicitly called out for leadership awareness.
body.Planned Activities:
EDI Migration to SAP – Next Steps
The project is now blocked on executive decisions, not technical readiness. The next steps are primarily governance and funding‑driven.
Immediate (Critical Path)

Funding decision on IT Resonance SOW

Dennis must identify and commit the funding source (~$30K).
This decision determines whether the project proceeds on a low‑risk or high‑risk path.


Legal decision on commercial tenant usage

Mike Bokermann to approve or deny use of the SAP commercial tenant for EDI‑only transactions.
Without approval, meaningful EDI work cannot begin until TPM is delivered in NS2 in Q3 2026.


Confirm go‑forward scenario

Leadership alignment required on whether the business is committing to:

Scenario 1 (recommended)
Scenario 2 (contingency; increased internal risk)
Scenario 3 (accept delay, cost exposure, and audit risk)





Near‑Term (Once Decisions Are Made)

If Scenario 1:

Onboard IT Resonance and finalize project schedule.
Begin AI‑assisted Sterling map conversion and commercial‑tenant configuration.
Target first customer go‑live in June 2026.


If Scenario 2:

Formally reallocate Johnny to near‑full‑time EDI migration work.
Accept that the end‑of‑year deadline becomes schedule‑sensitive with minimal buffer.


If Scenario 3:

Acknowledge that the SAP free‑license deadline will likely be missed.
Quantify and plan for $150K+ licensing exposure and extended Sterling operations.
body.Additional Comments:
The EDI Migration from IBM Sterling to SAP Integration Suite is strategically necessary, time‑bound, and financially constrained, with the December 31, 2026 deadline serving as a non‑negotiable forcing function.
Unlike many technical projects, the primary blocker is no longer technology—it is funding and legal authorization. The work required to migrate EDI maps, onboard partners, meet KPMG/SOX audit standards, and decommission Sterling is well understood. What differs across scenarios is who carries the execution risk and whether the company pays $30K now or absorbs $150K later.
Scenario 1 is the only path that:

Preserves internal team capacity
Provides a realistic, defensible delivery timeline
Maintains SOX and audit confidence
Avoids unbudgeted licensing costs

Scenario 2 is survivable but fragile, hinging almost entirely on Johnny’s uninterrupted availability and flawless execution.
Scenario 3 carries a high probability of cost overrun, audit exposure, and extended reliance on a platform already slated for retirement.
In short, the project is ready to move forward, but cannot progress until leadership resolves the funding and legal decisions. Further delay does not reduce cost or risk—it only compresses the schedule and forces the project toward higher‑risk outcomes.

body.Accomplished Activities:
Significant progress has been made since the last reporting period, with Phase 1 moving from active build into final validation and readiness.

Core CMDB foundation completed:

All three primary integrations — Intune, Azure, and Meraki — are live, stable, and ingesting data into ServiceNow.
No re‑architecture, redesign, or new tooling is required to complete Phase 1.


Azure integration stabilized and clarified:

Azure Local Appliances were reclassified as Windows Server, resolving a prior open leadership decision.
Linux server count discrepancy fully explained and resolved (final count confirmed at 41).
Windows Server attribute mapping tested and confirmed aligned with the Chemicals environment.


Meraki integration materially improved:

Device classification rules finalized and applied by model prefix (MS/C9, MR, MX, MG).
Device count reconciliation completed between raw Meraki inventory and CMDB.
A duplicate device name issue that blocked imports was fully resolved by confirming serial number and MAC address as the sole unique identifiers.
Meraki attribute payload matching completed and confirmed flowing correctly into ServiceNow.


CI quality and relationships strengthened:

CI‑to‑Asset relationships verified for core CI classes.
Previously misclassified CIs (e.g., abandoned VMs, generic resources, Veeam appliances) corrected.


Project scope and boundaries clarified:

Clayton Catalyst switches confirmed out of scope (managed under a separate CMDB initiative).
Offline and decommissioned Meraki devices will be retained in CMDB with non‑active status, aligned to CMDB lifecycle best practice.


Leadership decision backlog reduced:

Azure Local Appliance classification decision closed as of March 20.



Overall, the CMDB is now functionally built, with remaining work focused on validation, cleanup, documentation, and formal sign‑off rather than new development.
body.Planned Activities:
he project is now in its final Phase 1 close‑out stage, with progress dependent largely on leadership decisions and vendor accountability.
Near‑Term (Phase 1 Close‑Out)

Complete final data validation across Intune, Azure, and Meraki:

Attribute completeness and accuracy checks
Resolution of remaining classification edge cases


Finalize technical hardening items:

Complete attribute mapping transformations
Finalize unique identifier definitions by CI class
Lock IRE rules to prevent duplicate CI creation


Resolve remaining integration gaps:

Complete analysis and fix for Intune “Assigned To” field
Address remaining Meraki gaps (missing CIs, HTTP 308 behavior, offline device status updates)


Publish operational artifacts:

Final integration runbooks (Intune, Azure, Meraki)
Operating procedures for feeds, exclusions, and exception handling


Leadership decisions required to proceed:

Approve Phase 1 Definition of Complete
Select Phase 1 go‑live/sign‑off date (March 24–28 vs. by April 10)
Confirm scope lock (Intune, Azure, Meraki authoritative; Armis excluded)
Approve specialty device classification policy
Confirm Meraki stability window requirement (recommended 5–10 clean runs)



Vendor Accountability Actions

Deliver consolidated deliverables list to HCL and require HCL‑owned timeline
Provision admin access for HCL resources in lower environments
Address concerns regarding project management engagement, hours transparency, and proactive ownership

Once Phase 1 is formally signed off, Phase 2 can begin immediately, focusing on governance, data normalization, reporting, and process integration.
body.Additional Comments:
The CMDB Phase 1 implementation is technically complete and stable, with all foundational integrations in place and functioning as designed. The project has successfully transitioned from build to validation and operational readiness, and remaining work is primarily focused on quality assurance, documentation, and governance — not additional engineering.
The primary blockers at this stage are leadership decisions and vendor accountability, not system capability. Without clear sign‑off criteria and a confirmed go‑live date, Phase 1 risks remaining open‑ended despite being functionally ready.
Once leadership decisions are finalized and Phase 1 is formally closed, the program is well positioned to move into Phase 2 — shifting the CMDB from a functional inventory repository into a trusted operational backbone with governance, reporting, and process integration.
In summary:

Technical risk: Low
Execution risk: Moderate (vendor accountability)
Primary dependency: Leadership sign‑off and scope confirmation
Overall status: On track, pending decisions

body.Additional Comments:
Overall Summary — BSTS
BSTS is progressing well and nearly ready for cutover, with the primary technical blocker (AD access) resolved and verified. The remaining work is focused on final validation and deployment coordination, not system remediation. Once the test installation confirms database readiness, the application will be positioned to proceed with the planned early‑April cutovers with low overall risk.

Overall Summary — QDMS
QDMS remains in a hold state pending resolution of a fundamental technical dependency related to image storage. While a tentative April 19 cutover is defined, the schedule is explicitly conditional and may change based on validation results. The next step — testing real image upload and retrieval — is critical and will directly determine whether the project can proceed as planned or requires architectural remediation before go‑live.

Combined Program View (BSTS + QDMS)
BSTS is execution‑ready pending a final test installation and machine inventory confirmation, with low residual risk and near‑term cutover dates identified.
QDMS, by contrast, is not yet schedulable due to an unresolved technical constraint. Unlike BSTS, QDMS readiness hinges on the outcome of targeted validation testing rather than deployment coordination.
From a program standpoint:

BSTS is tracking toward early‑April closure.
QDMS is the higher‑risk, schedule‑sensitive item and will require close monitoring until its technical path is confirmed.

Recent Accomplishments

Meraki — Full CI ingestion achieved (March 27 — major milestone). IRE rules were implemented and fine-tuned, successfully discovering and reconciling all 10 previously missing Meraki CIs. Switch count is now confirmed at 223/223 ✓ and Wireless Access Points at 283/283 ✓ — both validated by the Network team. All four Meraki CI classes are fully reconciled.
Meraki Location attribute transform script deployed. A transform script was deployed to programmatically populate and normalize Location attributes for all Meraki CIs during data ingestion.
Intune attribute mapping document completed and distributed. The cmdb_ci_computer attribute mapping document was completed, shared with the Olin team for review, and next action items were discussed.
Intune CI count validated at 99% match. CI count confirmed against updated raw data — 1,955 of 2,005 records reconciled. The gap is the known assigned_to remediation effort, not a discovery issue.
Intune assigned_to root causes identified (March 25 working session). Approximately 900 of 2,026 enrolled devices are missing the assigned_to mapping. Root causes confirmed — split between bad upstream Intune data (admin accounts used for imaging, departed employee primaries, inactive user records) and a ServiceNow Transform Engine UPN domain-trimming bug. Remediation plan agreed and underway.
Azure cost center mapping and relationship modelling complete. Cost center attributes confirmed visible on both Linux and Windows servers. Relationship modelling for Windows and Linux servers validated and aligned with the Chemicals environment.
Meraki duplicate device name issue resolved. Serial number and MAC address confirmed as the sole unique identifiers — device names will no longer be used as a uniqueness criterion.

This is an open integration connectivity issue that requires Cisco Meraki's involvement to resolve. A follow-up joint Cisco Meraki/ServiceNow session is also still required. Allison Jackson and Michelle to coordinate.
Schedule Intune Triage Working Session — immediately. Shaham (HCL) needs to export the list of ~900 devices where assigned_to is empty (segmented by site). Michelle to schedule the 1-hour triage session with Ray, Austin, TJ, Jerome Bell, and the contractor within the next few days. A separate Intune coordination call also needs to be scheduled.
TJ / DSS teams to enforce imaging policy now. Admin accounts must stop being used to image devices — this is the root cause of a significant portion of the assigned_to gap. TJ to coordinate with Randy and Simba to enforce the policy before any further ServiceNow ingestion.
Meeting 2 (Olin internal alignment) must be scheduled. Michelle, Allison, and Tim need to align internally on the consolidated Phase 1/Phase 2 deliverables list before it is formally presented to HCL. This meeting is the gate that unlocks Meeting 3 (formal HCL deliverables review) — nothing moves on HCL accountability until this happens.
Meeting 3 (Formal HCL Deliverables Review) — blocked until Meeting 2 is complete. Once the internal list is aligned, Michelle will present the consolidated deliverables list to HCL technical leads and require HCL to propose their own delivery timeline. HCL does not get a date from the Olin team — they own their schedule.
Leadership decisions required to close Phase 1. Mike Guletz and the steering committee must approve the Definition of Complete, confirm the go-live date (Option A: week of March 24–28 / Option B: by April 10 / Option C: leadership-defined), confirm scope lock, approve the specialty device policy, and confirm the Meraki stability window. None of these have started.
body.Additional Comments:

All three core integrations — Microsoft Intune, Azure, and Meraki — are live and stable. The foundational build is done. Work has shifted from active development to final validation, documentation, and form alignment. Phase 1 cannot be formally closed out until leadership makes decisions on the Definition of Complete, go-live date, scope lock, and specialty device policy. No re-architecture or new tooling is required to close Phase 1 — the remaining work is cleanup, remediation, and sign-off.

body.Report Name: 5.4.2026 Sterling EDI to SAP Integration Suite
body.Accomplished Activities:
Recent Accomplishments as of 5.4.2026 Sterling EDI to SAP Integration Suite

Recent Accomplishments

Environment & Access — Fully Complete
•	SAP BTP / CPI access fully provisioned – all team members hold PI Admin roles.
•	Microsoft Teams channel active and all required members onboarded.
•	Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) configured with required applications behind the Olin firewall.
•	SAP schema and documentation extracted from SAP and distributed to the IT Resonance implementation team.

Build Artifacts — Completed
•	IDOC structures completed for all four active trading partner / document type combinations:
◦	Academy – 850 Purchase Order
◦	Canadian Tire – 850 Purchase Order
◦	Academy – Invoice
◦	Canadian Tire – Invoice
•	MIGs (Message Implementation Guidelines) created and simulated for all four document types above.
•	Communication partner configurations and MAGs (Mapping Application Guidelines) built within the SAP BTP IS tenant – showcased and confirmed in today’s session.

Mapping & Configuration — In Progress
•	Academy 850 inbound mapping work begun in SAP CPI – BEG, REF, and DTM segments underway, referencing IBM Sterling .map file for logic translation.
•	iFlow configuration progressing – PI Admin access issue was resolved; team is working from a copy of standard SAP iFlows.
•	B2B Integrator Map tool and mapping logic reviewed in detail during today’s session.
•	VAN communication relationship setup initiated – establishing the EDI intermediary connection for inbound/outbound file transfers with customers.
body.Planned Activities:
Next Steps
Connectivity Testing (Immediate Priority)
•	IDoc Connectivity — Ansel (IT Resonance) to notify Jonny Kenyon when the IDoc trace is “ON” in the BTP tenant so end-to-end IDoc connectivity testing can be initiated.
•	AS2 Connectivity — Jonny Kenyon to confirm whether AS2 messages can be triggered from the IBM VAN to the SAP BTP IS tenant.
•	Mendelson Feasibility — Assess whether the Mendelson open-source AS2 client can be installed on AVD for simulating inbound B2B scenarios and testing without requiring the live VAN.

Mapping Logic Completion & Review
•	Ansel and Hanu (IT Resonance) to revisit and finalize the B2B Integrator mapping logics, then schedule a review session with Jonny and the Olin team for validation and sign-off before implementation proceeds.
•	Hanu to complete Academy 850 inbound mapping (ANSI X12 → IDOC) in SAP CPI, working from the Sterling .map file. Covers BEG, REF, and DTM segments first.
•	Hanu to simulate the Academy 850 MIG against multiple PO test files to validate mapping logic, context handling, and segment segregation across varying data conditions.

VAN & End-to-End Testing Planning
•	Jonny / Team to confirm VAN relationship setup timeline: expected completion date and primary VAN contact.
•	Jonny and Hanu to define the first end-to-end data transfer test scenario once Academy 850 mapping is complete, including E1/E2 field population validation.
body.Additional Comments:
OVERALL SUMMARY
The EDI Migration project is transitioning Olin Winchester’s EDI processing from IBM Sterling B2B Integrator to the SAP BTP Integration Suite, with IT Resonance serving as the implementation partner. The target go-live for the first customer (Academy) is June 2026.

The project has successfully completed all foundational setup work — environment access, IDOC structures, initial MIG creation, and SAP schema distribution are all done. The team is now in the active build and configuration phase, focused on mapping logic, communication partner setup, and preparing for end-to-end connectivity testing between the IBM VAN and the SAP BTP tenant.

Key risk areas at this stage are the completion and review of mapping logic (which must be validated by the Olin team before finalization) and the resolution of IDoc and AS2 connectivity — both of which are actively being worked but not yet confirmed.

blockers were resolved this week: the IT Resonance purchase order was executed, and Legal approved use of the SAP commercial tenant, allowing work to begin immediately under the confirmed Scenario 1 approach (June 2026 first go‑live, full migration ahead of December 31 license deadline).

body.Additional Comments:
OVERALL SUMMARY
The EDI migration from IBM Sterling to SAP Integration Suite is officially underway. Two key blockers that had held the project in planning were resolved this week: the IT Resonance purchase order was executed (vendor formally onboarded) and Legal approved use of the commercial SAP tenant for EDI transactions. These two approvals clear the path for active development to begin immediately.

The active project path is Scenario 1 — the lowest-risk approach with a June 2026 first customer go-live target and full Sterling decommission by September 30, 2026, well ahead of the December 31 SAP license deadline. Bass Pro has been designated as the pilot partner and gates the first go-live milestone.

The IT Resonance kickoff meeting was held this week. Both teams aligned on scope (eight prioritized interfaces), working environment (commercial SAP tenant), timeline (seven-week engagement), roles, and next steps. An important dynamic to watch: Olin’s leadership made clear they expect a partner, not a vendor — flexibility and responsiveness from IT Resonance will be monitored throughout the sprint.

- Development complete for pilot go-live partners. Academy and Canadian Tire are technically ready at 95%, with IT Resonance having formally closed out development work.

body.Planned Activities:
07/13/2026 Next Steps
- Resolve the SAP outage — get a formal ETR from the SAP team and confirm system stability before any go-live execution.
- Get added to the SAP outage notification list — close the visibility gap so future outages are proactively communicated, not discovered after the fact.
- Confirm trading partner notification — get written confirmation that Academy and Canadian Tire have been formally notified of go-live, closing the loop Brandon was believed to be handling.
- Close CAB Submission & Approval — finalize approval for both partners; this is currently the main driver shifting the go-live target from Tuesday 7/14 to Wednesday 7/15.
- Hold the Go/No-Go Call — convene once SAP availability, trading partner notification, and CAB approval are all confirmed closed; render a formal Go/No-Go decision and lock the execution date.
- Execute go-live and hypercare — cutover for Academy and Canadian Tire, followed by Day-1 validation and stabilization monitoring, with no new changes introduced during hypercare.
- Close out IT Resonance handover — re-review documentation, confirm no outstanding gaps, and issue final sign-off.
- Advance Phase 1 rollout planning — keep Bomgaars, Midstates, NBS, Rural King, and Sports Inc. on track (targeting 8/2) in parallel, so the pilot go-live and SAP outage don't cost time on the broader 22-partner schedule.
body.Additional Comments:
CRITICAL UPDATE — SAP SYSTEM OUTAGE (as of Monday AM Standup, 7/13)
SAP has been down since Saturday, 7/11. As of this morning's standup, there is no estimated time of repair (ETR) available. Jonny reported the SAP team is apparently using the downtime to apply needed patches, but no formal communication or timeline has been shared with the project team.
Separately, it was noted in standup that we do not appear to be on any SAP outage notification distribution list — this needs to be corrected so the team is proactively alerted to future outages rather than learning about them after the fact.
Also new: Jonny is actively working the CAB tickets for both partners, and go-live execution now appears to be shifting to Wednesday, 7/15, to allow CAB approval to close properly.
Bottom Line for the Week
Academy and Canadian Tire are technically ready (95%) and development is complete, but the go-live date is now moving on two fronts. First, SAP has been down since Saturday 7/11 with no ETR as of this morning's standup, and go-live cannot proceed until the system is confirmed stable and available. Second, Jonny is actively working the CAB tickets for both partners, and closing CAB approval properly now appears to be pushing execution from Tuesday 7/14 to Wednesday 7/15. Customer Notification/Approval and the Go/No-Go Call still need to close this week, but the Go/No-Go decision must now account for both SAP availability and confirmed CAB approval — a formal Go cannot be issued until both are resolved. In parallel, Phase 1 rollout planning (Bomgaars, Midstates, NBS, Rural King, Sports Inc.) kicks off this week and should not be allowed to slip while attention is on the pilot go-live, the outage, and the CAB timeline.

body.Project Name: Sterling EDI to SAP Integration Suite
body.Report Name: 6.2.26 Sterling EDI to SAP Integration Suite
body.Accomplished Activities:
Connectivity & Infrastructure
Outbound AS2 communication is working. SAP BTP is successfully transmitting files to IBM VAN — files are decrypted, processed end-to-end, and the correct EDI IDs (Academy Sports) are resolving through the transformation layer. This was a major blocker that is now resolved.
AS2 certificate issue resolved. The root cause was a stale certificate at the agreement level in SAP BTP combined with a required deactivate/reactivate step that was not being performed. IBM re-engagement was explored and determined to be unnecessary — fix is owned by Jonny/IT Resonance.
API Gateway provisioned and approved. The API gateway architecture was identified, proposed, documented, and received leadership approval (Brandon Kamp and Dennis Bailey, June 1). Roles, access, and provisioning are complete. Only the endpoint creation and technical user association remain.
Mapping & Build
Templates created for 850, 810, 997, 856, and 860.
Partner profiles (inbound and outbound by customer) are set up.
IBM VAN customer mailbox setup complete.
Olin environment setup confirmed.
850 (Purchase Order) and 810 (Invoice) mapping substantially progressed; unit testing underway.
860 and 856 mapping approximately 50–60% complete.
Process Clarity
Confirmed that the WAP/custom flat file for Academy flows to customer service manually — not directly into SAP — which simplifies the SAP integration scope.
SIT and UAT confirmed as a single combined testing phase (one environment). UAT ownership assigned to Jonny; Laura's team plays a limited confirmation role.
Full end-to-end test scenario scope confirmed and documented for audit purposes.
Trading partner communication plan resolved — formal notification to Academy Sports and Canadian Tire not required since all testing is done via SPS Commerce EDI Portal.
body.Planned Activities:
Immediate (by EOD June 3)
Jonny: Fix ISA header character defect (double question marks → single "U") and run a clean re-test of outbound to IBM VAN.
Jonny: Complete API gateway endpoint creation and associate with internal technical user to activate inbound IBM VAN connectivity.
Peter (IT Resonance): Reconnect with Ansel; confirm 860 and 856 mapping progress and surface any blockers.
This Week (by EOW June 6)
IT Resonance: Complete 860 (Order Change) and 856 (ASN) mapping. Fallback target: June 9–10 if Ansel unavailable.
IT Resonance (Anu): Complete unit testing for 850 and 810.
IT Resonance: Confirm whether custom type system is achievable in TPM for flat file / 856 / 860 flows, or confirm process-direct approach.
Michelle: Receive and evaluate customer service response on WAP file format tolerance requirements.
Jonny/Brandon: Continue drafting the full trading partner timeline (target finalized by June 12 when Jonny is in Clay/St. Louis).
Week of June 9 — In-Person Working Session, St. Louis
Peter will be on-site. Goal is to run complete end-to-end test scenarios in one session: 850 in → WMS processing → 856 ASN out → 810 invoice out.
Brandon coordinating Riaz availability for Tuesday or Wednesday (June 10–11). Michelle booking room and calendar invite.
Testing & Closeout (following completion of mapping)
Run full end-to-end test suite; capture all output for audit record.
Data comparison: Sterling output vs. SAP Integration Suite output.
Map comparison: Sterling maps vs. SAP Integration Suite maps.
Obtain production data subset; run through cloud platform; compare outputs.
Capture formal approval of maps and data with Laura Hamilton (BPO).
Move into SIT/UAT signoff → Implementation → Go Live (target June 22–25 per project timeline).
body.Additional Comments: The overall project status is cautiously on track. Outbound AS2 connectivity is working, the certificate issue was resolved internally, and the API gateway decision was approved — all meaningful wins — but the June 5 build milestone is essentially today and mapping for 860 and 856 is only 50–60% complete, with the primary owner (Ansel) unavailable for two consecutive days and the team already floating a June 9–10 fallback. Unit testing for 850 and 810 is also incomplete, the custom flat file / TPM gap for 856 and 860 remains unresolved after two sessions, and inbound IBM VAN connectivity is not yet active. With the test phase scheduled to begin June 19 and go-live targeted for June 22–25, there is very little slack in the schedule — the project can stay on track, but only if mapping closes out by early next week and the in-person working session planned for the week of June 9 in St. Louis delivers the end-to-end test coverage needed to move into signoff.

The project has shifted away from the original plan to integrate financial systems into LeanIX using a single‑pane‑of‑glass dashboard. Instead, we are aligning with LeanIX’s upcoming Contract Management feature, which is expected to be released in early Q2 2026. This new capability will allow us to store financial information directly on LeanIX Fact Sheets, expanding opportunities for future integrations and utilizing better TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) reporting.

Current Status:
- Monitoring LeanIX’s Contract feature rollout timeline (early Q2 2026).
- Documenting required financial data fields for use within the new Fact Sheet structure.
- Paused work on dashboard integration to prevent rework.

Benefits of the New Approach:
- Shortens development time—less custom features need added/maintained.
- Improves data quality and governance by keeping financial info native within LeanIX.
- Enhances use cases such as app rationalization, portfolio insights, and cost transparency.
- Reduces dependency on external dashboards and reduces long‑term overhead.

body.Additional Comments: The goal is to make the new approach as scalable and automated as possible. Based on early observations, it appears the only level of manual updating will be in mapping each contract to leanix. This is much less labor intensive than our previous approach, which required manual allocation of $ when mapping applications to contracts. This new approach should have the calculations in LeanIX drive most or all of the computations based on a single contract dollar amount.

Recent Accomplishments
●	Executed the weekend cutover, migrating the QDMS database to Azure SQL via the SqlPackage command-line tool (export, compression to backup file, and import).
●	Resolved a first-attempt import failure caused by a 32 GB default size cap by adjusting the size parameter and resending the import.
●	Diagnosed a subsequent stall at the "Updating database" phase (~28–30 GB of an ~80 GB database) using SQL DMV queries against the target Azure SQL database, rather than cancelling prematurely — correctly identifying that low local network activity reflected the bulk transfer finishing and index-rebuild work moving server-side, not a frozen process.
●	Identified the likely root cause of the stall (the RebuildIndexesOfflineForDataPhase=True setting combined with a 4-vCore Azure SQL compute tier) and prepared a scale-up plan (GP_Gen5_4 to GP_Gen5_8/16) to accelerate index rebuilding without restarting the migration.
●	Resolved an unrelated provisioning error during the same window by removing the affected account from the local admins group, shifting the issue fully to Conditional Access.
●	Completed Intune-reporting remediation on the flagged Oxford critical machines in parallel with the database migration, keeping both workstreams moving simultaneously.
●	Stood up a formal QDMS Post-Migration Issue Log (with severity/status tracking, dashboard summary, and instructions) to capture and manage hypercare issues going forward.
●	Triaged a live post-migration access issue for Repco (unable to access QDMS): verified network path to the QDMS host, staged a manual installer on OLINSCCM12, and engaged network/security support (Ray Dees, Optiv) via the hypercare bridge.

body.Additional Comments:
CURRENT STATUS as of 130pm 6/2/2026
Based on the latest testing results and issues identified, we have made the decision to pull back slightly from broad user testing and move into a more controlled stabilization phase.

While we have made meaningful progress on performance improvements, including reduced latency and confirmation of root cause (application-level, not infrastructure-related),  New regression issues introduced with the latest build (including system freezing during Customer Complaint creation) have impacted core functionality and limited our ability to proceed with broader UAT.

With the object of ensuring we are providing a clean, stable environment before requesting further end-user validation – 

We will temporarily transition to IT-led System Integration Testing (SIT) only 
 The internal IT/technical team will: 
•	Execute and validate all test cases end-to-end
•	Work through and filter out defects, regressions, and environmental issues
•	Stabilize both functionality and performance before re-engaging the business users

Once we reach an acceptable level of stability:
             We will: 
•	Re-engage business users for full regression/UAT retesting
•	Require complete re-execution and documentation of test cases
This will provide: 
•	Clear validation of system readiness
•	Confidence that both performance and functionality meet expectations

We will not proceed with a formal system upgrade or cutover decision until
•	SIT is complete and stable 
•	End-user testing has been successfully revalidated 
•	All critical issues are resolved or have approved mitigation plans

We will focus on timing being driven by system readiness, not target dates.  We are prioritizing stability, quality and confidence in the system before moving forward with the cutover.

Imported ~30,000 asset records into the CMDB, validating ingestion end‑to‑end.
Identified that previous ingestion included entire enterprise data, and began refining imports to ensure Ammo‑specific filtering only.

Data Quality & Asset Scope Refinement

Initial review of imported data identified irrelevant asset classes (media devices, network adapters, medical devices, etc.) and marked them as candidates for removal.
Established guiding principle: Only assets with business value, compliance impact, or critical data should be tracked. Guest network devices are excluded.

Compliance Engagement Initiated

Identified the need to align asset scope with CMMC Level 2 / Level 3 requirements.
Meeting scheduled with Adam Barletter and Nathan Faith (2/16/26) to validate compliance‑driven expectations.
Recognized assets containing or touching CUI as potential mandatory inclusions.

Azure → SN Reconciliation Review

Investigated VM import inconsistencies between Azure and ServiceNow, including server count mismatches.
Identified classification issues and “noise” entries (e.g., those starting with VBA) for removal.
Confirmed Azure as the authoritative source for virtual servers; Armis to serve as source for additional asset categories.

Initial Process & Tooling Alignment

Reviewed task and user story tracking options; aligned on using PPM 360 for current visibility.
Validated that the immediate technical issue with imports was resolved, allowing reconciliation work to proceed.
body.Planned Activities:
Data Filtering & Asset Class Decisions

Continue filtering Armis‑imported data to remove non‑relevant or noisy asset types.
After meeting with compliance leads (Adam & Nathan), finalize which asset classes remain in scope.

Reconciliation & Import Validation

Re‑run all import schedules in sequence and validate results.
Compare CMDB server counts with the latest validated Azure server list to confirm completeness.
Escalate to Gideon or Maverick if server discrepancies persist.

Define Asset Ownership & Support Roles

Clarify ownership boundaries with HCL for asset management responsibilities, ongoing updates, and data maintenance.
Confirm how to handle non‑networked but business‑critical assets that Armis is unable to detect.

Improved Data Management

Continue data normalization efforts to reduce duplicates and improve record consistency.
Investigate feasibility of targeted imports for specific IP ranges (noting current connector limitations).

Governance & Tracking

Refine approach for tracking work items; review additional tooling options if PPM 360 becomes insufficient.
Maintain monitoring case open to support continued oversight of SN → CMDB import health.
body.Additional Comments:
Discovery Source Flipping:
Azure and Armis may update the same records, causing Discovery Source to toggle — strong reconciliation rules will be required to prevent overwriting authoritative data.


CUI Data Sensitivity:
As compliance levels increase (potential move toward Level 3), additional OT and business‑critical systems may enter scope. Decisions made now should anticipate future compliance requirements.


Not All Detected Devices Are Assets:
Armis detection does not equate to CMDB asset qualification; a curated approach is essential to avoid unnecessary data volume and CMDB clutter.


Guest Network Devices:
Should remain out of scope; tracking these introduces unnecessary overhead with limited value.


Operational Load:
High initial data volume demonstrates the importance of strict filters and ongoing governance to prevent performance impacts and data sprawl.


Upcoming Meeting Dependencies:
Compliance guidance from Adam and Nathan will influence:

Asset class retention/removal
Scope of device categories
Required reconciliation rules
How Ammo devices map to CMMC requirements

body.Additional Comments:
High-Level Summary
This week marked a major shift in the project’s integration strategy. The team collectively agreed to deprecate the Armis connector due to persistent data quality issues and pivot to a more reliable architecture centered on Azure, Microsoft Intune, and Meraki. The Azure connection is already live, and the team is now progressing into guided setup, verification, and POC phases for the Intune and Meraki connectors. This change positions the project to improve CMDB accuracy, data completeness, and long-term maintainability.
